deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a sequence of programmatic and philosophical notes on mathematics and its relation to physics, in the same aphoristic style as the neighbouring folios.

(1) Continuation of a sentence begun on another page. Paraphrase: someone who does geometry but ignores the fine experiments of Michelson (interferometry), Nernst (heat theorem) and Laue (X-ray diffraction, 'Diamantgitter', i.e. diamond lattice) is like a reactionary politician. He stubbornly, bureaucratically and orthodox-historically draws a line and does not do physics. He is also like someone who eats only field crops and scorns fine game or the results of the finest cuisine. The opening of this sentence appears to be the last lines of the folio supplied here as the NEXT page ('Wer heutzutage sich nur auch immer an die Experimente hält, dass durch 3 Stützpunkte die Ebene festgelegt ist ... und dem gemäss nur'). That suggests the folio order or numbering is reversed or disturbed.

(2) 'Mathematics is thinking, pure thinking, nothing further, i.e. definite, correct thinking, thinking as such.'

(3) A prophecy: once mathematics has conquered all the border provinces, pure analysis will enjoy a flowering such as it has never experienced. Hilbert's example is the principle of integrating infinitely many differential equations at once, as at the core of statistical mechanics. There one does not wish to know the individual integrals (solutions) of the ODE system. Even if general integration were possible and the ordinary integration business completed, one would not yet have the desired answer, and the work might not even be eased. The parenthetical gives a name for this 'collective' kind of integration; the word is hard to read.

In modern terms (my gloss): for a Hamiltonian system dq_i/dt = dH/dp_i, dp_i/dt = -dH/dq_i with N -> infinity, one replaces solving the trajectories by studying invariant measures or phase-space densities. That means Liouville's equation d(rho)/dt + {rho, H} = 0, Gibbs ensembles rho ~ exp(-H/kT), and averages of observables. These are integrals over phase space rather than integrals of the ODEs.

(4) Repeated prophecy: from the connection with physics, especially statistical mechanics, mathematics will flourish as never before. The suggested programme is the same collective integration applied to differential, integral and functional equations 'in the infinite setting' (infinitely many unknowns).

(5) A heuristic principle of mathematical physics: consider the extreme, trivial cases and vary them, i.e. perturb around limiting cases.

Dating hints: the references to Laue and the diamond lattice (Bragg structure of diamond, 1913) place the note at about 1913 or later.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no computation. The only issue is structural: the first sentence is grammatically incomplete. It seems to continue the final lines of the folio given as 'next page', so the catalogue order of [94] and its neighbour may be inverted.

results.what: Statistical mechanics viewed as 'integration' of infinitely many ODEs in which individual solutions are irrelevant and only collective (ensemble) behaviour matters; programme to extend this to differential, integral and functional equations in infinitely many variables
results.modern_name: Ensemble or ergodic approach: Liouville equation, Gibbs measures, invariant measures, later statistical solutions of PDEs / infinite-dimensional analysis
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1838), Boltzmann, Gibbs (1902); later Birkhoff and von Neumann (ergodic theorems, 1931); Hopf and Foias (statistical solutions, 1950s-70s)

results.modern_name: Hilbert's programme for axiomatizing physics (6th problem); his kinetic gas theory work (1912)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (1900 problems, 1912 Boltzmann equation papers, 1930 Königsberg address)

deep.surprise_reason: These are programmatic remarks fully consistent with Hilbert's known views: the unity of mathematics and physics, the 6th problem, his 1912 work on kinetic gas theory and the infinite-variable integral-equation programme, and the 1930 'Naturerkennen und Logik' address. The image of 'integrating infinitely many ODEs' as the core of statistical mechanics anticipates later talk of statistical solutions only rhetorically, with no mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The Hamiltonian vector field is divergence-free (Liouville's theorem), the basis of the phase-space-density approach alluded to (my gloss, not on page). Should equal 0.
The Gibbs density exp(-beta*H) has vanishing Poisson bracket with H, so it is stationary under the flow (gloss). Should equal 0.
